neighbours.label: the verb slot opened by an enabling construction (leaves you free to, far enough that X could, be able to, enough space to): the complement of a phrase that grants room or capacity, as opposed to a plain infinitive of wanting or deciding
fire: Outsourcing the payroll leaves your managers free to plan the next season.
The lid opens wide, giving you enough room to slide in a full-size tray.
He leaned back from the map far enough so that he could read the coastline.
With the chores done early, the children were able to spend the afternoon outside.
A larger kitchen would give us the space to cook for the whole family.
Their savings left them free to travel for most of the year.
Moving the meeting online means everyone will be able to attend from home.
She held the photo back far enough that her grandmother could see it clearly.
quiet: The outsourcing firm sent your managers a plan for the next season.
The lid is painted blue and has a small handle on the top.
He leaned over the map and pointed at the coastline with a pencil.
With the chores done early, the children decided to watch a film.
A larger kitchen was the main reason we bought the house.
Their savings were kept in a bank account in another town.
Moving the meeting online was the manager's idea from the start.
She held the photo in her lap while her grandmother told the story.
